Context: The system in the body that controls when a person needs to sleep, eat, and perform other basic functions is called the internal clock. It is controlled by the brain.
Title: Source 2: Nature resets body's clock
Author: by Meghan Rosen
Content: A short camping trip could help people rise and shine, researchers report. After a `text(week)` living in tents in Colorado's Rockies, campers' internal clocks shifted about `text(two hours)` earlier. It transformed even night owls into early birds...

A master clock in the brain controls the release of melatonin. This `ultext(hormone)` prepares the body for sleep. Melatonin levels rise in the early evening and then `ultext(taper off)` in the morning before a person wakes up.

But many people today spend their `text(days)` indoors and their nights [absorbed] in the glow of electric lights (including the light emitted by TVs and computers). Too little early morning light and too much evening lighting can throw the body's clock out of sync. This unnatural lighting can trigger the body to ramp up melatonin levels later at night. It can also lead the hormone levels to fall later than normal in the morning—often after a person has woken up. Lingering levels of this sleep hormone can make people groggy.

Kenneth Wright Jr., a sleep researcher at the University of Colorado, Boulder, and colleagues whisked eight volunteers away for a summer camping trip. After nightfall, the campers used only campfires for lighting. No flashlights (or cellphones) allowed.

`text(Each day)`, the campers soaked up `text(four)` times as much light as they got indoors. They also went to sleep and naturally woke up more than an `text(hour)` earlier than they had before the trip.

Tests done after the volunteers got home again showed that their melatonin levels now climbed around sunset. They also petered out at sunrise — `text(two hours)` earlier than before they had gone camping...
“Start your `text(day)` off with a morning walk, and open the [window] shades to expose yourself to sunlight,” Wright advises.

:box:`bbtext(Glossary)`

hormone: a substance produced naturally inside the body that affects how a body grows

taper off: gradually become weaker or smaller

petered out: came to an end
